title: Each source has a freshness lifetime from its own change history, and a lookup revalidates only sources past it
goal: A source's freshness lifetime is computed with no network from its own history: the Poisson rate of its observed changes (the changed_utc values across the git history of _fetch_state.csv, or its mapped Learn file's commits) where it has two or more, else a fraction (RFC 9111's typical 10%) of the time since its content date, else its provider's default; fetch.py --status prints each source's lifetime and age; kb_pack and kb_ask.py revalidate a cited source automatically only when its age exceeds its lifetime, printing the stale stamp meanwhile (stale-while-revalidate, D-gmrjivyw); the hook stays offline; the suite tests the estimate on a planted history.

notes: Premise: no tool estimates a source's change rate today; _fetch_state.csv keeps only the latest checked_utc and changed_utc, so the history lives in git (git log -p kb/public/_fetch_state.csv). The first step measures, per host, how many sources have two or more recorded changes, and states the share the Poisson estimate can serve before the fallback. Sources: RFC 9111 heuristic freshness (S-ods72iyh), RFC 5861 stale-while-revalidate (S-m7xkty3c), the Poisson change model (S-7uckhkxr), all in public/agents/doc-change-detection.md, Freshness at question time. Decision D-gmrjivyw. Planned 2026-10-12: premise reproduced (no lifetime, Poisson or change-rate code in fetch.py, factdiff.py, provider.py or census.py). The freshness_lifetime test runs fetch.py --status on a planted git history and drives kb_pack and kb_ask.py with a stubbed revalidation, asserting the hook path makes none.
